newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa finishes below 900 as stg rises.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa finishes below 900 as stg rises.

text.p: London cocoa futures ended weaker after early gains were stifled by sterling's recovery.
"There was a bit of consolidation from yesterday's gains and a steadier pound probably helped to stick it back," said one trader.
Traders noted brisk two-way trade in March 1997/March 1998 spread on good buying on the distant March.
By the morning close, near March was eight stg down at 896 stg a tonne after touching a high of 906.
"Cocoa keeps trying to break through the 900 convincingly but it never does," said one

Technically, immediate support and resistance is seen at 890 and 910 respectively. Second-position May was 10 stg lower at 914 while the active March/May spread was last traded at 18 stg. Distant March shed nine stg at 970 after a high of 980.
The day's volume reached a modest 5,045 lots.
Sterling firmed against dollar and mark in early Europan trading, recovering from sharp drop on Thursday in the wake of tumble in UK stock market and gilts.
The sterling-denominated London cocoa market had been hammered in the past weeks by origin sellers taking advantage of recent sterling strength.
There was no fresh news affecting prices but traders said a series of European and U.S. fourth quarter grinding data due in the coming two weeks could inspire a new market direction.
